claim: Mutations in NFU1 and BOLA3 have been linked to genetic diseases with defects in mitochondrial Fe-S centers.
source: Mutations in NFU1 and BOLA3 have been linked to genetic diseases with defects in mitochondrial Fe-S centers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to patient studies throughout the manuscript.

claim: Nfu1 functions in a late step of [4Fe-4S] cluster biogenesis that is of heightened importance during oxidative metabolism.
source: Through genetic studies in yeast, we demonstrate that Nfu1 functions in a late step of [4Fe-4S] cluster biogenesis that is of heightened importance during oxidative metabolism.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic studies in yeast showing Nfu1's role and its importance during oxidative conditions.

claim: Nfu1 physically interacts with components of the ISA [4Fe-4S] assembly complex and client proteins that need [4Fe-4S] clusters to function.
source: Proteomic studies revealed Nfu1 physical interacts with components of the ISA [4Fe-4S] assembly complex and client proteins that need [4Fe-4S] clusters to function.
evidence: This is supported by proteomic data and co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: Bol1 functions earlier in Fe-S biogenesis with the monothiol glutaredoxin, Grx5.
source: Additional studies focused on the mitochondrial BolA proteins, Bol1 and Bol3 (yeast homolog to human BOLA3), revealing that Bol1 functions earlier in Fe-S biogenesis with the monothiol glutaredoxin, Grx5
evidence: This is supported by interaction studies and proteomic data showing Bol1-Grx5 association.

claim: Bol3 functions late with Nfu1.
source: Bol3 (yeast homolog to human BOLA3), revealing that Bol1 functions earlier in Fe-S biogenesis with the monothiol glutaredoxin, Grx5, and Bol3 functions late with Nfu1.
evidence: This is supported by genetic and proteomic studies showing Bol3 association with Nfu1 and [4Fe-4S] client proteins.

claim: Nfu1, assisted by Bol3, functions to facilitate Fe-S transfer from the biosynthetic apparatus to the client proteins preventing oxidative damage to [4Fe-4S] clusters.
source: Given these observations, we propose that Nfu1, assisted by Bol3, functions to facilitate Fe-S transfer from the biosynthetic apparatus to the client proteins preventing oxidative damage to [4Fe-4S] clusters.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data showing Nfu1's importance during oxidative stress and its interactions with ISA complex and client proteins.

claim: Patients with Multiple Mitochondria Dysfunctions Syndrome (MMDS) are afflicted with lactic acidosis, nonketotic hyperglycinemia and infantile encephalopathy typically leading to death in their first year of life.
source: Patients with this Multiple Mitochondria Dysfunctions Syndrome (MMDS) are afflicted with lactic acidosis, nonketotic hyperglycinemia and infantile encephalopathy typically leading to death in their first year of life.
evidence: This is stated as a clinical description of MMDS patients and is supported by citations to patient studies.

claim: The MMDS syndrome is associated with an impairment of lipoic acid-dependent 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases arising from defective lipoate synthesis and defects in respiratory complexes I and II in select tissues including muscle and liver.
source: The syndrome is associated with an impairment of lipoic acid-dependent 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases arising from defective lipoate synthesis and defects in respiratory complexes I and II in select tissues including muscle and liver.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of MMDS and is supported by citations to patient studies.

claim: The deficiency in protein lipoylation in MMDS is due to impaired activity of lipoic acid synthetase, which requires two [4Fe-4S] cluster cofactors.
source: The deficiency in protein lipoylation is due to impaired activity of lipoic acid synthetase, which requires two [4Fe-4S] cluster cofactors (Hiltunen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the requirement of [4Fe-4S] clusters for lipoic acid synthetase.

claim: The hyperglycinemic phenotype in MMDS arises from failed lipoylation of the glycine cleavage enzyme.
source: The hyperglycinemic phenotype arises from failed lipoylation of the glycine cleavage enzyme.
evidence: This is stated as a mechanistic explanation for the hyperglycinemia observed in MMDS patients.

claim: IBA57 and ISCA2 are known components of the ISA complex, along with ISCA1, which functions in the formation of [4Fe-4S] clusters within mitochondria.
source: Whereas IBA57 and ISCA2 are known components of the ISA complex, along with ISCA1, which functions in the formation of [4Fe-4S] clusters within mitochondria (Mühlenhoff et al., 2011; Gelling et al., 2008; Sheftel et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies establishing the ISA complex composition and function.

claim: The functions of NFU1 and BOLA3 in Fe-S cluster assembly remain an enigma.
source: the functions of NFU1 and BOLA3 in Fe-S cluster assembly remain an enigma.
evidence: This is stated as the motivation for the study, indicating a gap in knowledge at the time of the research.

claim: Yeast cells lacking Nfu1 are partially compromised in mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] cluster formation, but the defect is not as pronounced as in cells lacking components of the ISA complex.
source: Yeast cells lacking Nfu1 are partially compromised in mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] cluster formation, but the defect is not as pronounced as in cells lacking components of the ISA complex (Isa1, Isa2 and Iba57) (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011; Schilke et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies and is supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: Yeast nfu1∆ cells have diminished protein lipoylation levels.
source: As in patient cells with mutations in NFU1, yeast nfu1∆ cells have diminished protein lipoylation levels (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation and is confirmed by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Humans and yeast have two mitochondrial BolA proteins termed BolA1 (Bol1 in yeast) and BolA3 (Bol3 in yeast).
source: Humans and yeast have two mitochondrial BolA proteins termed BolA1 (Bol1 in yeast) and BolA3 (Bol3 in yeast) (Cameron et al., 2011; Willems et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies identifying these proteins.

claim: Little is known concerning the physiological function of BolA proteins.
source: but little is known concerning their physiological function.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge, motivating the investigation of BolA proteins in this study.

claim: The similarities of phenotypes in patients with MMDS mutations in NFU1 and BOLA3 suggest that BOLA3 may likewise function in mitochondrial Fe-S biogenesis.
source: The similarities of phenotypes in patients with MMDS mutations in NFU1 and BOLA3 suggest that BOLA3 may likewise function in mitochondrial Fe-S biogenesis (Cameron et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on clinical observations with a citation.

claim: Fe-S cluster synthesis within the mitochondria occurs on a scaffold complex and preformed clusters are subsequently transferred to recipient proteins.
source: Fe-S cluster synthesis within the mitochondria occurs on a scaffold complex and preformed clusters are subsequently transferred to recipient proteins (Lill et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a review.

claim: The initial cluster formed is a [2Fe-2S] cluster assembled on the ISU scaffold complex consisting of five proteins, Nfs1, Isd11, Yfh1, Yah1 and Isu1 (or Isu2; yeast nomenclature).
source: The initial cluster formed is a [2Fe-2S] cluster assembled on the ISU scaffold complex consisting of five proteins, Nfs1, Isd11, Yfh1, Yah1 and Isu1 (or Isu2; yeast nomenclature) (Lill et al., 2012; Schmucker et al., 2011; Tsai and Barondeau, 2010; Lange et al., 2000; Webert et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: The sulfide ions are provided by the Nfs1 cysteine desulfurase, along with its effector proteins Isd11 and Yfh1.
source: The sulfide ions are provided by the Nfs1 cysteine desulfurase, along with its effector proteins Isd11 and Yfh1 (Tsai and Barondeau, 2010; Lill and Mühlenhoff, 2008; Gerber et al., 2003; Biederbick et al., 2006; Bridwell-Rabb et al., 2014; Parent et al., 2015; Fox et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: Assembled [2Fe-2S] clusters on Isu1 are transferred to the monothiol glutaredoxin Grx5 through the action of the Ssq1 ATPase and the DnaJ protein Jac1.
source: Assembled [2Fe-2S] clusters on Isu1 are transferred to the monothiol glutaredoxin Grx5 through the action of the Ssq1 ATPase and the DnaJ protein Jac1 (Ciesielski et al., 2012; Majewska et al., 2013; Uzarska et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Two [2Fe-2S] clusters transferred by Grx5 are condensed into a [4Fe-4S] cluster on the downstream ISA complex (Isa1, Isa2 and Iba57) prior to transfer to client proteins.
source: Two [2Fe-2S] clusters transferred by Grx5 are condensed into a [4Fe-4S] cluster on the downstream ISA complex (Isa1, Isa2 and Iba57) prior to transfer to client proteins (Mühlenhoff et al., 2011; Gelling et al., 2008; Sheftel et al., 2012; Brancaccio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Nfu1 has been implicated to function as a late Fe-S maturation factor in bacteria and fungi.
source: Nfu1 has been implicated to function as a late Fe-S maturation factor in bacteria and fungi (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011; Bandyopadhyay et al., 2008; Py et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: Nfu1 has been proposed as an alternate scaffold protein for cluster synthesis.
source: an alternate scaffold protein for cluster synthesis (Cameron et al., 2011; Tong et al., 2003)
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis from previous studies with citations.

claim: Nfu1 has been proposed as a persulfide reductase associated with the sulfide transfer.
source: or as a persulfide reductase associated with the sulfide transfer (Liu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis from a previous study with a citation.

claim: The lack of NfuA in Escherichia coli and Azotobacter vinelandii is associated with decreased viability under stress conditions.
source: The lack of NfuA in Escherichia coli and Azotobacter vinelandii is associated with decreased viability under stress conditions (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2008; Py et al., 2012; Angelini et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to bacterial studies.

claim: E. coli NfuA and human Nfu1 are two domain proteins with the C-terminal domain containing the functionally important CxxC motif that is known to bind a [4Fe-4S] cluster at a homodimer interface.
source: E. coli NfuA and human Nfu1 are two domain proteins with the C-terminal domain containing the functionally important CxxC motif that is known to bind a [4Fe-4S] cluster at a homodimer interface (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2008; Tong et al., 2003; Angelini et al., 2008; Gao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Recombinant expression and purification of Azotobacter NfuA or human Nfu1 did not result in Fe-S cluster bound to the purified protein.
source: Recombinant expression and purification of Azotobacter NfuA or human Nfu1 did not result in Fe-S cluster bound to the purified protein, but in vitro Fe-S reconstitution studies followed by Mössbauer spectral studies demonstrated the presence of a [4Fe-4S] cluster (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2008; Py et al., 2012; Tong et al., 2003; Angelini et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous biochemical studies.

claim: In vitro Fe-S reconstitution studies followed by Mössbauer spectral studies demonstrated the presence of a [4Fe-4S] cluster in Azotobacter NfuA or human Nfu1.
source: but in vitro Fe-S reconstitution studies followed by Mössbauer spectral studies demonstrated the presence of a [4Fe-4S] cluster (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2008; Py et al., 2012; Tong et al., 2003; Angelini et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous biochemical studies.

claim: Synechocystis NifU was reported to bind a [2Fe-2S] cluster.
source: Synechocystis NifU was reported to bind a [2Fe-2S] cluster (Yabe et al., 2004; Nishio and Nakai, 2000), but Mössbauer spectral studies were not done to validate the assignment.
evidence: This is stated with citations but noted as not fully validated.

claim: The ability of bacterial NfuA to transfer its cluster to apo-aconitase in vitro is consistent with a role in a late step of cluster transfer.
source: The ability of bacterial NfuA to transfer its cluster to apo-aconitase in vitro is consistent with a role in a late step of cluster transfer (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2008; Angelini et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to in vitro studies.

claim: BolA proteins are known to coordinate Fe-S clusters in conjunction with monothiol glutaredoxins.
source: BolA proteins are also known to coordinate Fe-S clusters in conjunction with monothiol glutaredoxins (Li and Outten, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: One of the three BolA proteins in Arabidopsis thaliana BolA1 was shown to bind a [2Fe-2S] cluster in a complex with glutaredoxin (Grx).
source: One of the three BolA proteins in Arabidopsis thaliana BolA1 was shown to bind a [2Fe-2S] cluster in a complex with glutaredoxin (Grx) (Roret et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: The cluster associated with the BolA:Grx complex is coordinated by two thiolate ligands, one from Grx and the other from an associated glutathione, and two histidine ligands from BolA1.
source: The cluster associated with the BolA:Grx complex is coordinated by two thiolate ligands, one from Grx and the other from an associated glutathione, and two histidine ligands from BolA1.
evidence: This is stated as a structural description based on previous studies.

claim: The cytosolic BolA2 proteins of yeast and humans coordinate [2Fe-2S] clusters at the heterodimer interface with monothiol glutaredoxins.
source: Likewise, the cytosolic BolA2 proteins of yeast and humans coordinate [2Fe-2S] clusters at the heterodimer interface with monothiol glutaredoxins (Li and Outten, 2012; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: BolA proteins are found only in aerobic species.
source: BolA proteins are found only in aerobic species (Willems et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: Depletion of the mitochondrial BolA1 in HeLa cells caused an oxidative shift in the mitochondrial thiol/disulfide redox ratio.
source: Depletion of the mitochondrial BolA1 in HeLa cells caused an oxidative shift in the mitochondrial thiol/disulfide redox ratio (Willems et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: S. cerevisiae cells lacking the mitochondrial Nfu1 protein (nfu1∆ cells) are markedly impaired in growth on synthetic complete medium with acetate as a carbon source.
source: S. cerevisiae cells lacking the mitochondrial Nfu1 protein (nfu1∆ cells) are markedly impaired in growth on synthetic complete medium with acetate as a carbon source (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A drop-test assay.

claim: nfu1∆ cells display only a slight growth impairment on glycerol/lactate medium, suggesting a partial respiratory growth defect that is exacerbated with acetate as the carbon source.
source: However, the mutant cells display only a slight growth impairment on glycerol/lactate medium, suggesting a partial respiratory growth defect that is exacerbated with acetate as the carbon source.
evidence: This is stated based on the growth assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: nfu1∆ cells exhibit specific but partial defects in the formation of [4Fe-4S] clusters analogous to phenotypes seen in patients with mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome.
source: It was previously reported that nfu1∆ cells exhibit specific but partial defects in the formation of [4Fe-4S] clusters analogous to phenotypes seen in patients with mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011; Schilke et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: Aconitase and succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) activities are markedly impaired in nfu1∆ yeast cells, yet residual activity persists.
source: We confirmed the defects in [4Fe-4S] client enzymes reported for nfu1∆ cells showing that aconitase and succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) activities are markedly impaired, yet residual activity persists (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B enzymatic activity data.

claim: Aconitase activity is markedly attenuated in nfu1∆ yeast cells, whereas its activity is not significantly depleted in human nfu1 patients.
source: Aconitase activity is markedly attenuated in nfu1∆ yeast cells, whereas its activity is not significantly depleted in human nfu1 patients (Cameron et al., 2011; Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to patient studies, comparing yeast and human phenotypes.

claim: No defect was observed in the yeast nfu1∆ mutant in respiratory complex III, cytochrome bc1, which requires a [2Fe-2S] cluster in its Rieske Rip1 subunit.
source: No defect was observed in the yeast mutant in respiratory complex III, cytochrome bc1, which requires a [2Fe-2S] cluster in its Rieske Rip1 subunit or in cytochrome oxidase that requires a [2Fe-2S] cluster in Yah1 for heme a formation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B enzymatic activity data.

claim: No defect was observed in the yeast nfu1∆ mutant in cytochrome oxidase that requires a [2Fe-2S] cluster in Yah1 for heme a formation.
source: No defect was observed in the yeast mutant in respiratory complex III, cytochrome bc1, which requires a [2Fe-2S] cluster in its Rieske Rip1 subunit or in cytochrome oxidase that requires a [2Fe-2S] cluster in Yah1 for heme a formation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B enzymatic activity data.

claim: Lipoic acid (LA) conjugates on pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) and oxoglutarate dehydrogenase (KDH) were attenuated in nfu1∆ cells.
source: Consistent with the known defects of nfu1∆ yeast cells and human nfu1 patients, lipoic acid (LA) conjugates on pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) and oxoglutarate dehydrogenase (KDH) were attenuated in nfu1∆ cells (Figure 1C) (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 1C immunoblotting data.

claim: Steady-state protein analysis by SDS-PAGE showed diminished Sdh2 levels in nfu1∆ cells, the Fe-S subunit of SDH.
source: Steady-state protein analysis by SDS-PAGE showed diminished Sdh2 levels, the Fe-S subunit of SDH.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C immunoblotting data.

claim: Sdh2 contains three distinct Fe-S clusters ([2Fe-2S], [4Fe-4S], and [3Fe-4S] clusters), which transfer electrons from the catalytic Sdh1 subunit to ubiquinone.
source: Sdh2 contains three distinct Fe-S clusters ([2Fe-2S], [4Fe-4S], and [3Fe-4S] clusters), which transfer electrons from the catalytic Sdh1 subunit to ubiquinone.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Sdh2 structure and function.

claim: In the absence of Fe-S cluster insertion, Sdh2 stability is compromised.
source: In the absence of Fe-S cluster insertion, Sdh2 stability is compromised (Kim et al., 2012) (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is stated with a citation and supported by the reduced Sdh2 levels shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The aconitase protein stability is not dependent on the presence of its [4Fe-4S] cluster.
source: In contrast, the aconitase protein stability is not dependent on the presence of its [4Fe-4S] cluster (Gelling et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: Two enzymes involved in yeast lysine biosynthesis Aco2 and Lys4 contain [4Fe-4S] clusters.
source: Two enzymes involved in yeast lysine biosynthesis Aco2 and Lys4 contain [4Fe-4S] clusters (Fazius et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: Yeast lacking the ISA complex are auxotrophic for lysine and accumulate homocitrate as a metabolic intermediate.
source: Whereas yeast lacking the ISA complex are auxotrophic for lysine and accumulate homocitrate as a metabolic intermediate, nfu1∆ cells propagate normally in medium lacking lysine and do not accumulate homocitrate as shown by GC-MS metabolomic studies (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated based on metabolomic data (not shown) and contrasts ISA complex mutants with nfu1∆ cells.

claim: nfu1∆ cells propagate normally in medium lacking lysine and do not accumulate homocitrate.
source: nfu1∆ cells propagate normally in medium lacking lysine and do not accumulate homocitrate as shown by GC-MS metabolomic studies (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated based on metabolomic data (not shown).

claim: Sufficient [4Fe-4S] cluster synthesis and distribution occurs in nfu1∆ cells for lysine synthesis.
source: Thus, sufficient [4Fe-4S] cluster synthesis and distribution occurs in nfu1∆ cells for lysine synthesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that nfu1∆ cells grow normally without lysine supplementation.

claim: In a screen using transformants with a high-copy yeast DNA library, respiratory competent vector-borne clones of nfu1∆ BY4741 cells containing NFU1, ISA2, and the YAP2 transcriptional activator were isolated.
source: In a screen using transformants with a high-copy yeast DNA library, we isolated respiratory competent vector-borne clones of nfu1∆ BY4741 cells containing NFU1, ISA2, and the YAP2 transcriptional activator.
evidence: This is stated as a result of a genetic screen.

claim: Overexpression of Isa2 was the only ISA component capable of partially restoring respiratory growth of nfu1∆ cells on acetate medium.
source: Although Isa2 is a component of the mitochondrial ISA heterotrimeric complex comprised of Isa1, Isa2 and Iba57, overexpression of Isa2 was the only ISA component capable of partially restoring respiratory growth of nfu1∆ cells on acetate medium (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A drop-test assay.

claim: ISA2 transformants of nfu1∆ cells showed a partial restoration lipoylation of KDH and SDH activity.
source: ISA2 transformants of nfu1∆ cells showed a partial restoration lipoylation of KDH and SDH activity suggesting that the respiratory capacity of the mutant cells was partially restored by elevated Isa2 levels (p value ~0.14) (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: The respiratory function of Nfu1 can be partially replaced by super-physiological levels of the Isa2 component of the ISA complex.
source: Thus, the respiratory function of Nfu1 can be partially replaced by super-physiological levels of the Isa2 component of the ISA complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the suppression data showing ISA2 overexpression rescues nfu1∆ phenotypes.

claim: Affinity purification of Nfu1-Strep with Strep-Tactin beads showed co-purification of Isa1 and Isa2.
source: Affinity purification of Nfu1-Strep with Strep-Tactin beads showed co-purification of Isa1 and Isa2 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1F immunoblotting data.

claim: Nfu1 associated with three [4Fe-4S] client proteins Aco1, Aco2 and Lys4, but not the [2Fe-2S] client protein Rip1.
source: In addition to the interaction with Isa1 and Isa2, Nfu1 associated with three [4Fe-4S] client proteins Aco1, Aco2 and Lys4, but not the [2Fe-2S] client protein Rip1 (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1G and H immunoblotting data.

claim: The partial respiratory function of nfu1∆ cells was restored by overexpression of Yap2 or its paralogue Yap1.
source: The partial respiratory function of nfu1∆ cells was also restored by overexpression of Yap2 or its paralogue Yap1 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A drop-test assay.

claim: Yap1 and Yap2 are transcriptional activators that induce the expression of a battery of antioxidant genes, including thioredoxin, thioredoxin reductase and glutathione reductase, in response to oxidative stress.
source: Yap1 and Yap2 are transcriptional activators that induce the expression of a battery of antioxidant genes, including thioredoxin, thioredoxin reductase and glutathione reductase, in response to oxidative stress (Fernandes et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cells with the YAP transcription factors showed restoration of LA-associated PDH.
source: To confirm that the suppression of nfu1Δ cells by the YAP transcription factors was specifically due to a recovery of the [4Fe-4S] centers, we analyzed mitochondria from the transformants to test for restoration of lipoic acid conjugates of PDH and KDH and observed a clear restoration of LA-associated PDH (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A immunoblotting data.

claim: The identification of YAP1 and YAP2 as high copy suppressors of nfu1Δ cells suggested a role for Nfu1 during oxidative stress.
source: The identification of YAP1 and YAP2 as high copy suppressors of nfu1Δ cells suggested a role for Nfu1 during oxidative stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the genetic suppression data.

claim: The respiratory growth of nfu1Δ cells was partially restored with the addition of the antioxidants, GSH and N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) to the growth medium.
source: Consistent with this postulate, the respiratory growth of nfu1Δ cells was partially restored with the addition of the antioxidants, GSH and N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) to the growth medium (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B drop-test assay.

claim: Nfu1 has a role during oxidative metabolism.
source: These results support a role for Nfu1 during oxidative metabolism.
evidence: This is inferred from the suppression by antioxidants and YAP transcription factors.

claim: Anoxic nfu1Δ cells did not exhibit a significant difference between WT and nfu1Δ cells in SDH and aconitase activities and lipoic acid adducts.
source: As previously described normoxic nfu1Δ cells exhibited the expected marked attenuation in SDH and aconitase activities and reduced lipoic acid adducts; however, the anoxic cells did not exhibit a significant difference between WT and nfu1Δ cells (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Anoxic WT cells showed a marked reduction in mitochondrial enzymatic activities and steady-state protein levels compared to normoxic WT cells (~30% of normoxia).
source: It should be noted that anoxic WT cells showed a marked reduction in mitochondrial enzymatic activities and steady-state protein levels compared to normoxic WT cells (~30% of normoxia), yet anoxic nfu1Δ cells did not show a marked further attenuation in SDH and lipoic acid conjugates.
evidence: This is stated based on the data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Cells are more dependent on Nfu1 during oxidative metabolism.
source: Thus, the cells are more dependent on Nfu1 during oxidative metabolism.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of normoxic and anoxic conditions.

claim: Nfu1 consists of two domains in addition to the N-terminal mitochondrial targeting sequence (MTS) based on sequence homologies.
source: Nfu1 consists of two domains in addition to the N-terminal mitochondrial targeting sequence (MTS) based on sequence homologies (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A schematic.

claim: The N-terminal domain (NfuN, residues 22–126) is only conserved within eukaryote species.
source: The N-terminal domain (NfuN, residues 22–126) is only conserved within eukaryote species, while the C-terminal NifU-like domain (NfuC, residues 143–256) is widely conserved in all species and contains the important the Fe-S binding CxxC motif (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The C-terminal NifU-like domain (NfuC, residues 143–256) is widely conserved in all species and contains the important the Fe-S binding CxxC motif.
source: while the C-terminal NifU-like domain (NfuC, residues 143–256) is widely conserved in all species and contains the important the Fe-S binding CxxC motif (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Cells containing only the Nfu1 NfuC domain were capable of respiratory growth on either glycerol/lactate or acetate medium.
source: Cells containing only the Nfu1 NfuC domain were capable of respiratory growth on either glycerol/lactate or acetate medium (Figure 3B), whereas cells harboring only the Nfu1N domain failed to propagate.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B drop-test assay.

claim: Cells harboring only the Nfu1N domain failed to propagate on respiratory medium.
source: whereas cells harboring only the Nfu1N domain failed to propagate.
evidence: This is stated based on the drop-test assay shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Cells with the NfuC, but not the NfuN, domain showed normal Sdh2 and lipoic acid levels.
source: Additionally, cells with the NfuC, but not the NfuN, domain showed normal Sdh2 and lipoic acid levels.
evidence: This is stated based on the immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The NfuN domain was well expressed in cells, unlike the functional C-terminal domain that was markedly attenuated in protein stability.
source: Although the NfuN domain failed to restore Nfu1 function, the fragment was well expressed in cells, unlike the functional C-terminal domain that was markedly attenuated in protein stability (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C immunoblotting data.

claim: The functionality of the NfuC domain suggests that only minimal levels of Nfu1 are important for function.
source: The functionality of the NfuC domain suggests that only minimal levels of Nfu1 are important for function.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the poorly expressed NfuC domain is functional.

claim: Cells harboring Nfu1 with the two CxxC cysteinyl residues replaced by alanines exhibited a respiratory growth defect analogous to nfu1Δ cells suggesting a loss-of-function phenotype.
source: Cells harboring Nfu1 with the two CxxC cysteinyl residues replaced by alanines exhibited a respiratory growth defect analogous to nfu1Δ cells suggesting a loss-of-function phenotype (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The critical role of the CxxC motif cysteines was previously shown in the E. coli NfuA.
source: The critical role of the CxxC motif cysteines was previously shown in the E. coli NfuA (Angelini et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a previous study.

claim: A conserved glycine just upstream of the CxxC motif is commonly mutated to a cysteine in patients with MMDS.
source: A conserved glycine just upstream of the CxxC motif is commonly mutated to a cysteine in patients with MMDS (Navarro-Sastre et al., 2011; Nizon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to patient studies.

claim: The G>C mutant that mimics the MMDS1 patient allele displayed a severe synthetic sick phenotype on glycerol/lactate medium.
source: The most striking substitution was the G>C mutant that mimics the MMDS1 patient allele, which displayed a severe synthetic sick phenotype on glycerol/lactate medium (Figure 3D).
